subject: Clarify: non-training commitment & retention windows for end-to-end transcripts

Subject: Quick Q on 'we do not train on your data' + transcript retention

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — helpful stuff. A couple of follow-ups from our security team that I wanted to get clarified before we move forward with a pilot: they want an explicit statement about "we do not train models on our data" and then a clear breakdown of what you actually retain and for how long for (request logs, full transcripts, cached KV, audit logs). Two specific asks: 1) a plain-English definition of your non-training guarantee and any edge cases, and 2) retention windows for each artifact type and the deletion workflow (API or ticket, expected SLA).

Can you point me to any compliance artifacts we can share with FinLend Legal? They asked for something they can add to their SOC 2 evidence pack.

Thanks,
Samir

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-12T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on 'we do not train on your data' + transcript retention

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear ask, and great to meet you on the demo. I pulled in Rishi (Privacy) and Jasmine (Support/Operations) to make sure we capture policy + operational steps.

Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer-provided content from production inference requests to train or update our base models by default. That includes prompts, completions, and attachments submitted via the hosted API. There are a few operational nuances below that your security team usually asks about.

What "not used for training" means at Redwood (plain English):
- We do not ingest customer content from production inference calls into any internal training corpora or fine-tuning pipelines unless a customer explicitly opts in via a documented contract amendment.
- We may derive aggregated, de-identified telemetry (e.g., token latency distributions, error rates) for service quality improvements; that telemetry cannot be traced back to individual user content and is not used to train model weights.
- Data used for research or product R&D is pulled only from datasets where we have explicit consent or from public/open sources; production customer data is excluded unless explicitly consented.

Retention / artifact breakdown (typical Hosted defaults):
- Full request & response transcripts (complete payloads): retained by default for 30 days for debugging, incident investigation, and abuse detection. Customer-configurable retention: 0 days / 7 days / 30 days / custom via contract.
- KV cache / inference ephemeral state: ephemeral by design; persisted only for the duration of the session plus up to 24 hours in the cache layer for performance. Not used for long-term analytics or training.
- Request metadata & telemetry (timestamps, latency, error codes): retained 365 days for billing and service analytics; aggregated copies used for product metrics.
- Audit logs (admin actions, key rotation, policy changes): retained 730 days to satisfy enterprise compliance needs.
- Attachments submitted to support (manual upload to help debug an issue): retained until the support case is closed plus 90 days; we can delete earlier on request.

Deletion workflow:
- Self-serve: customers on Dedicated/Private can set retention policies in the Console and trigger per-route deletion.
- API: Hosted customers can call the Data Deletion API (POST /v1/customers/{id}/requests/delete) to request deletion of transcripts and related artifacts; typical automated processing SLA is 48 hours for standard deletion requests.
- Manual: For legal/forensic deletions that require certification, file a Support case (attach the deletion request) and we will issue a signed deletion certificate within 7 business days.

Edge cases & clarifications:
- Opt-in training: customers can opt in to share data for model improvements; this is always contractually scoped and auditable. Opt-in data is stored separately and flagged for training use only after explicit agreement.
- Aggregated safety signals: content may be used to surface safety policy changes (e.g., new moderation rules) but only in an aggregated, non-identifiable form.
- Private deployments: for VPC/on-prem customers, we do not access customer content; retention is managed by the customer's infra and Redwood's control plane only stores metadata necessary for orchestration (subject to contract).

I attached a short retention matrix and our non-training assertion PDF for your legal team. Rishi / Jasmine — please add anything I missed or correct retention default numbers if out of date.

Next steps: Samir, does FinLend want the standard 30-day transcript retention or a different default for the pilot? We can include a clause in the SOW to set a custom retention window if needed.

Best,
Grace

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-13T08:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on 'we do not train on your data' + transcript retention

Hi Samir — quick follow from privacy: two operational notes to make the assurance airtight for your auditors.

1) Evidence bundle: we can provide the following artifacts for SOC 2 evidence: the non-training assertion PDF (signed), an excerpt of the data flow diagram showing separation of telemetry vs content, and a copy of our retention configuration page for the pilot tenant. I attached the PDF and retention-matrix CSV to this thread.

2) Verified deletion: when a deletion request is completed we record a deletion event in the customer's audit log (timestamp + operator id). For higher-assurance requests we will provide a signed deletion certificate (PDF) with the list of deleted object ids (or hashed ids) and a processing timestamp. Production SLA for the certificate is 7 business days once the deletion job completes.

Operational proposal for FinLend pilot:
- Set transcript retention to 7 days for the pilot (reduced risk for early evaluation).
- Retain telemetry/metrics for 1 year for billing/observability; provide access to aggregated exports only.
- Enable the Data Deletion API for your security team and share the API key lifecycle plan.

If that sounds good, I can draft the SOW language and Jasmine will configure the pilot tenant.

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi Samir — I'm looping in the Ops steps so we can move quickly.

Action items I will take:
- Create the pilot tenant and set transcript retention to 7 days by default.
- Share a one-time signed non-training assertion PDF and the retention matrix (attached).
- Provision a scoped API key for the Data Deletion API and send instructions for rotating/retiring the key after the pilot.
- Document the deletion ticket flow and attach the template for your auditors so they can see the certificate format.

If you'd like the deletion certificate to include hashed ids for each deleted object, confirm and we'll enable that option (adds 1-2 business days to certificate issuance).

I'll start the tenant provisioning today and follow up once it's ready.

Best,
Jasmine
